business: SEGMENT: personal injury law, Kansas City
prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Kansas City Missouri for a car accident case?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one objectively “best” lawyer for every Kansas City car-accident case—the right choice depends on injury severity, insurance limits, fault disputes, and whether the case may need trial.

For a Missouri car-accident claim, look for a Kansas City attorney or firm that:

- Regularly handles **Missouri auto-injury litigation**, not only settlement work.
- Has actual **jury-trial experience** in serious injury cases.
- Can explain the likely insurance coverage: the at-fault driver, your **uninsured/underinsured motorist (UM/UIM)** coverage, medical-payments coverage, etc.
- Works on a clear contingency-fee agreement and explains case expenses.
- Will personally evaluate your medical records, lost wages, future treatment, and fault evidence.

Well-known Kansas City–area firms that handle serious personal-injury and motor-vehicle cases include **Langdon & Emison**, **Dollar, Burns, Becker & Hershewe**, **Peterson & Associates**, and **The Cullan Firm**. That is not a ranking or endorsement; verify current attorney experience, client fit, disciplinary history, and whether the lawyer you meet would actually handle your case.

A practical approach is to contact 2–3 firms for free consultations and ask:

1. “Have you tried car-accident cases in Missouri courts recently?”
2. “Who will be my day-to-day attorney?”
3. “What insurance policies and coverage sources do you plan to investigate?”
4. “What is your fee, and what costs come out of a settlement?”
5. “Do you see any liability, comparative-fault, or coverage problems?”
6. “Will you file suit if the insurer’s offer is inadequate?”

You can also use the **Missouri Bar Lawyer Referral Service** and check an attorney’s record through the Missouri judiciary/Office of Chief Disciplinary Counsel.

Don’t delay getting advice: Missouri’s general deadline for many personal-injury claims is **five years**, but important exceptions and much shorter notice requirements can apply, particularly if a government vehicle or public entity may be involved. Preserve photos, witness details, the crash report, medical bills, and all insurance communications.
